# Sakka Saṁyutta (SN 11)

**ID:** SN 11
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Sakka Saṁyutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0301m.mul10.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The collection has extensive parallels across early Buddhist literature, with twenty-six discourses mapped to corresponding texts in the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (SĀ / T 99, split between fascicles 40 and 46) and the 'other' *Saṁyuktāgama* (SĀ² / T 100 / BZA), alongside parallels in the *Ekottarikāgama* [Bingenheimer]. Individual discourses show wide circulation: the protective *Dhajagga Sutta* (SN 11.3) parallels versions in the Tibetan *Mahāsūtras* (D 292, *Dhvajāgra-nāma-mahāsūtra*), while Prajñāvarman's commentary on the *Udānavarga* (*Udānavargavivaraṇa*, D 4100) preserves a parallel to the *Vepacittisutta* (SN 11.4) [Bingenheimer; Skilling].
